llm.summary: This React skill is a conventional coding-guidance package with disclosed local preference memory and no evidence of hidden, destructive, or data-exfiltrating behavior.

dimensions.detail: The requested node binary and React project scaffolding commands are proportionate for a React development skill and are not automatic or hidden.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill itself is Markdown metadata and guidance, but setup examples include mutable npx/npm commands such as create-next-app@latest, vite@latest, shadcn@latest, and unpinned npm installs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The setup guidance leans toward Next.js despite the manifest saying routing and deployment specifics belong to the nextjs skill; this is a scope-quality mismatch, not a security concern.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses persistent user preferences and project memory under ~/Clawic/data/react/; this is purpose-aligned and skill-scoped, though users should avoid storing secrets there.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts provide React component, state, forms, testing, performance, and migration guidance consistent with the declared React development purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Safe to install as a React guidance skill. Before running the optional setup commands, consider pinning package versions and running scaffolding in a normal least-privileged project environment; do not put secrets in the skill memory file.
llm.findings:
[P2] expected: The flagged HTML comments in memory-template.md are ordinary template annotations about project decisions, not hidden instructions to override the agent or perform unauthorized actions.
[SDI-1] expected: The Next.js recommendations are somewhat broader than the stated exclusion for Next.js routing/deployment, but they are visible React stack guidance and do not introduce hidden or privileged behavior.
[RP1] expected: The unpinned npx commands are real supply-chain exposure if a user runs them, but they are disclosed setup examples for common React tooling rather than automatic skill behavior.
[T08] expected: The static finding correctly identifies mutable third-party package execution in setup examples; this warrants user caution and version pinning, not a Review verdict by itself.
